correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the Boolean synchronous rule as sigma_v(t+1)=sgn(((A+I/2)sigma(t))_v). Symmetry gives a strictly decreasing finite two-time energy whenever sigma(t+2) differs from sigma(t), so eventual periods <=2. Classifying fixed configurations by number of mixed parts leaves two unanimous states plus all-even half-filled families. On a genuine two-cycle, a part is stationary or flips homogeneously; one oscillating part is impossible, two require equal sizes and a strict middle binomial band on the stationary part, three require a uniquely strictly largest part. This yields P1=2+all-even*prod binom(n_i,n_i/2), P2=1_{unique maximum}+sum_{i<j,n_i=n_j} B(n_i,n_k), and dynamical zeta denominator (1-z)^P1(1-z^2)^P2. Independently enumerated every labelled state for the 27 size triples a,b,c=1..3 and confirmed fixed and primitive two-cycle counts.

value.rationale: The exact number of all recurrent states and primitive oscillations, not just a universal period bound, is a natural invariant of deterministic majority on labelled networks. It exhibits a sharp arithmetic symmetry transition: pairwise distinct sizes have precisely one primitive two-cycle, whereas equal-sized pairs permit entire binomial families of oscillating communities with an unchanged third part.

limitations: Three strictly positive part sizes, synchronous loopless complete tripartite majority with keep-on-tie only.
No basin counts or sharp transient lengths.
The 1983 paper was not fully accessible.
